skill.name: implementing-with-tdd
skill.description: Guide agents through test-first implementation in PairCoder projects, including task status updates, pytest checks, linting, and completion steps.
skill.summary: Apply a red-green-refactor workflow for PairCoder code changes.

content.value_statement: Code changes can drift without clear test coverage. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through a PairCoder TDD workflow.
actual_capabilities: Guides task status updates before and after implementation.
Defines a red, green, refactor sequence for code changes.
Lists pytest commands for focused tests, full tests, coverage, and failed tests.
Documents project test naming and fixture conventions.
Includes ruff lint checks and an aggregate PairCoder CI command.
limitations: Assumes the repository uses PairCoder project commands.
Focuses on Python testing with pytest and ruff.
Does not generate tests or implementation code by itself.
References a separate task lifecycle skill for final completion.

use_cases.title: Add a Feature Safely
use_cases.description: Use the skill to write a failing test, implement the feature, and verify the green result.

use_cases.title: Fix a Regression
use_cases.description: Use the skill to reproduce a bug with a targeted test before changing production code.

use_cases.title: Standardize Agent Workflows
use_cases.description: Use the skill to keep AI coding sessions aligned with PairCoder testing and task completion rules.

prompt_templates.title: Start a TDD Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the implementing-with-tdd skill for TASK-123. Identify the smallest failing test before changing implementation code.

prompt_templates.title: Fix a Bug Test First
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the implementing-with-tdd skill to fix this bug. First add a regression test that fails for the current behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Implement and Verify
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the implementing-with-tdd skill to implement this change, run the focused pytest command, then run lint checks.

prompt_templates.title: Complete a Full TDD Cycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the implementing-with-tdd skill for this feature. Show the red test, minimal implementation, refactor decision, and final checks.

output_examples.input: Add validation for invalid task identifiers.
output: A failing regression test is identified first.
The implementation is scoped to the validation path.
Focused tests and lint checks are run before completion.

output_examples.input: Fix a command parsing bug in the PairCoder CLI.
output: The task is moved to in-progress status.
A targeted parser test captures the bug.
The green test result is followed by project checks.

output_examples.input: Prepare a feature for task completion.
output: The aggregate CI command is used for final verification.
Task completion follows the project lifecycle process.

best_practices: Write the smallest failing test that proves the required behavior.
Run focused tests before broader project checks.
Keep refactors separate from behavior changes when possible.
anti_patterns: Do not implement production code before defining the expected test failure.
Do not mark tasks complete before tests and linting pass.
Do not ignore project fixture and naming conventions.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps agents follow a test-first workflow for PairCoder code changes.

faq.question: Which test framework does it assume?
faq.answer: It assumes pytest for tests and ruff for linting.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance and example commands for an agent or developer to use.

faq.question: Can I use it outside PairCoder?
faq.answer: Parts of the TDD workflow apply elsewhere, but task commands are PairCoder-specific.

faq.question: Does it replace code review?
faq.answer: No. It improves test discipline but does not replace review or project approval.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it when a bug fix, feature, or refactor benefits from clear test coverage.
